headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU can ingest document content via MCP/API, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no shared write or network surface, limiting pairwise harm.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can ingest local documents and exposes an MCP Server, so attacker-controlled document content could be treated as instructions if routed into a permissive downstream workflow. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no input surface, so the pairwise pathway is one-way and limited to whatever orchestrator bridges them.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded into an instruction-following agent or MCP tool chain without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF the orchestrator copies document text from MinerU into python-cheatsheet prompts, malicious instructions in the document can be executed logically.
mitigations: Disable MCP routing for untrusted documents.
Add provenance tags to MinerU outputs before passing them onward.
Strip instruction-like text from extracted content.
Use a fixed schema between agents instead of raw text.
requires-engineering: add content-safety filtering at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, and OCR text, but python-cheatsheet has no files, APIs, or network egress. There is no shared workspace or obvious exfiltration path in the profiles, so leakage risk is limited unless an external orchestrator copies sensitive extracts into B.
conditions: IF an external workflow copies MinerU-extracted sensitive text into python-cheatsheet prompts, that content can appear in B's outputs.
IF both agents are placed in a shared workspace by the operator, document contents may be exposed through manual handling.
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs in a separate workspace.
Avoid pasting extracted text into python-cheatsheet.
Redact sensitive fields before handoff.
Use local-only storage for intermediate artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries in the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU has no filesystem write, git, shell, or subprocess capability, and python-cheatsheet likewise has no write or network surface. With no overlapping mutable resource access, there is no plausible capability conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would change.
IF either profile is extended with git or filesystem write permissions, overlapping mutation could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Avoid granting git or database credentials.
Run them under separate service accounts.
requires-engineering: add lock-based coordination if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU can produce extracted text and structured document outputs, but python-cheatsheet is a reference/documentation agent with no action-taking authority or network egress. The pair can still cascade errors if B blindly republishes MinerU output, but the blast radius is limited to content quality rather than external actions.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is used to rewrite MinerU output without verification, extraction errors can be propagated.
IF an external system treats B's text as authoritative, downstream misinformation can spread.
mitigations: Require human review of MinerU extracts.
Add citation/traceability fields to B's outputs.
Compare extracted facts against source documents.
Use confidence labels on derived text.
requires-engineering: add automated verification against the original file.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles: MinerU is documented as private/fully offline and python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no data classes touched. There is no PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive flow shown, so a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into an external workflow, compliance analysis must be revisited.
IF either agent is deployed with logging or retention outside the shown profiles, residency or retention issues could arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Confirm logging settings before deployment.
Document retention for intermediate artifacts.
Use local-only execution for sensitive documents.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data classes.
